FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Cement 
Matrix Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


Fibre cement lightweight concrete sandwich panel is produced under ambient conditions having density 
between 500 kg/m? and up to 1 000 kg/m?, and primarily used for the construction of non-load bearing 
partition walls. Some of the advantages of these panels are lightness of construction, faster speed of work 
compared to brick masonry. 


This standard covers manufacturing, performance and quality requirements of the completed panel. This 
standard also covers standard connection and joinery materials necessary for testing. The standard specifies the 
components for the sandwich wall panel that consist of two fibre reinforced cement facing sheets of nominal 
thickness in range of 4 mm to 6 mm thickness on either sides of a lightweight concrete core. These panels have 
a unique jointing system that facilitates rapid construction and are fully cured at the factory itself. 


The concealing work for internal electric conducting and plumbing, etc are not recommended with these fibre 
cement lightweight concrete sandwich panels in view of the limitation of thickness of the sheet. 


In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international coordination among the standards 
and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in the country. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex С. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 *Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision) . The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17908 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


FIBRE CEMENT SHEET — LIGHTWEIGHT CONCRETE 
SANDWICH PANELS — SPECIFICATION 


1SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements of fibre cement 
sheet namely lightweight concrete sandwich panels 
having density up to 1 000 kg/m’. These panels are 
primarily used for the construction of non-load bearing 
partition walls. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated in Annex A. 


3 CONSTRUCTION, DIMENSIONS AND 
TOLERANCES 


These panels are manufactured by use of two fibre 
reinforced cement facing sheets of nominal thickness of 


TYPICAL JOINTING 
SYSTEM 


22 
г 


2 
y 
2 
22 


4 mm to 6 mm, on either sides of a lightweight concrete 
core. These panels are manufactured with jointing 
system that facilitates rapid construction. Typical 
construction details of sandwich panels with jointing 
system are shown in Fig. 1. Edges of the sandwich 
panel may be manufactured with square edges as per 
Fig. 2, or recess edges as per Fig. 3. 


The nominal dimensions of the panels are so designed 
that, taking account ofthe thickness ofthe facing sheets, 
they should produce wall lengths and heights which 
conform to the principle of modular coordination. The 
dimensions of sandwich panel shall be as given in 
Table 1 with the tolerances as given in Table 2. 

NOTE — Other shape, size and jointing system may also be 

manufactured as per the agreement between manufacturer and 

purchaser.

4.2 Cement 
Any of the following type of cement shall be used: 
a) Ordinary Portland cement conforming to IS 269, 


b) Rapid hardening Portland cement conforming to 
IS 8041, 

c) Sulphate resisting Portland cement conforming to 
IS 12330, 

d) Portland pozzolana 
IS 1489 (Part 1), and 


е) Portland slag cement conforming to IS 455. 


4.3 Pulverized Fuel Ash 


Pulverized fuel ash conforming to IS 3812 (Part 1) with 
minimum fineness 300 m?/kg, may be used, if cements 
enumerated in 4.2(a) to (c) are used and provided 
uniform blending with cement is ensured. 


cement conforming to 


4.4 Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag 


Ground granulated blast furnace slag conforming 
IS 16714 may be used. 


4.5 Fibres 


a) Discreet elements like cellulose fibres, synthetic 
fibres, mineral fibres, etc which are randomly 
dispersed, 


b) Continuous strands and tapes, and 
c) Nets or webs. 


4.6 Water 


The water used in the manufacture of the sandwich 
panels shall be free from matter harmful to concrete or 
reinforcement, or matter likely to cause efflorescence 
in the units and shall meet the requirements of IS 456. 


4.7 Aeration Agent 


The aeration agent shall be of such chemical composition 
that is capable of producing stable aeration cells in 
concrete, which can resist the physical and chemical 
forces imposed during mixing, transporting, pumping, 
placing and setting of concrete. The aeration agent 
should meet the requirements of 9 of IS 9103 and the 
aeration produced shall be stable for duration beyond 
the final setting time of Portland cement. Such agents 
shall be completely harmless to concrete and embedded 
steel reinforcement and be nontoxic, non-flammable 
and biodegradable. 


4.8 Additives 


Additives as enlisted below may be added as and when 
required: 


a) accelerating, water-reducing admixtures 
conforming to IS 9103, 
b) integral cement waterproofing compound 


conforming to IS 2645, and colouring pigments, 
c) gypsum as per IS 1290, 


IS 17908 : 2023 


d) gypsum building plaster - excluding premixed 
lightweight plasters as per IS 2547 (Part 1), 


e) gypsum building plasters - premixed light 
weight plasters as per IS 2547 (Part 2), 


f) byproduct gypsum as per IS 12679, 


g) plaster of Paris as per IS 2547 (Part 1) and IS 2547 
(Part 2), 


h) vermiculite, and 
j) Perlite expanded polystyrene beads. 


NOTE — Where no Indian Standards apply, the additives 
shall be shown by test or experience, not to be detrimental 
to the durability of the sandwich panel. The compatibility 
of admixtures with each other and with other ingredients in 
the mix should be determined by tests as agreed between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser. 


5 MANUFACTURE 


5.1 Raw Material Mix 


The raw material mix design indicating the proportions 
of various ingredients should be worked out carefully 
keeping in view the desired physical properties of the 
finished panels. 


5.2 Batching 


The quantities of various ingredients should be 
proportioned on the basis of their mass weight, with 
due correction being made to the quantity of solid 
ingredients on account of their inherent moisture 
content. 


5.3 Mixing 


The ingredients shall be mixed in a mechanical 
mixer. The dry ingredients like reinforcement fibres, 
aggregates, fly ash, cement and other additives shall be 
fed into the mixer first and thoroughly mixed to ensure 
even distribution of cement. The appropriate amount 
of water shall be added thereafter continuing the 
mixing. The aerating agent, which is made by blending 
the aerating agent concentrate, water and with or 
without compressed air in predetermined proportions, 
calibrated for a specific discharge rate, shall be added 
in measured amount to the slurry of cement, fly ash, 
fiber and water in the batch mixer as prepared above. 
After an additional mixing to get uniform consistency, 
the slurry form of foamed cellular concrete of desired 
wet unit weight shall be ready to be poured out into 
forms/moulds, etc. 


These materials shall then be poured and sandwiched 
between a pair of fibre cement facing sheets which shall 
be separated and supported by using conventional jigs 
and fixtures. 


The adhesion between the core material and fibre 
cement sheets is achieved by inorganic bonding with 
core material while manufacturing the sandwich panel. 
The panels so prepared shall be allowed to harden for 


IS 17908 : 2023 


a predetermined period and thereafter jigs/fixtures shall 
be separated. The panels shall be cured by retaining 
the humidity of the composite by wrapping the 
composite with polymeric films or by water curing or 
air curing. 


5.4 Moulds 


Gang moulds of required sizes and thickness may 
be constructed either of wood, steel, rigid plastics, 
aluminum or other acceptable materials. The mould 
surfaces should be pre-coated with an approved *mould 
releasing agent' to ensure proper surface finish. The 
fibre reinforced cement sheets are inserted in each 
mould. These moulds shall be fixed on trollies. After 
insertion of cement sheets trolley shall be locked with 
two tie rods on each side. 


5.5 Conveying and Placing 


АП equipments for conveying and placing, whether 
manual, like wheel barrows or big buckets, or 
mechanical equipment like mortar pumps, should be of 
such size and design and used in such a manner as to 
ensure proper placing and formation of the sandwich 
panel. Aerated concrete is a fluid mass and due to the 
absence of coarse aggregate and the ball bearing effect 
of minute foam bubbles, the fluid mass of aerated 
concrete fills up and levels into moulds by itself without 
the need of external vibration or compaction. 


5.6 De-moulding of Cast Elements 


Depending on the ambient temperature and property of 
cement used, the panels may be de-moulded within 24 h 
from pouring of aerated concrete unless accelerated 
curing processes are used. 


5.7 Curing 


This curing shall be done by humid curing or air curing 
method. Panels can be dispatched after attaining the 
required strength.

6 PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 General 


All panels shall be solid, voids free, be sound and free of 
cracks or other defects which interfere with the proper 
placing of units or impair the strength or performance 
of the construction. Minor chipping resulting from 
customary methods of handling during delivery, shall 
not be deemed to be ground for rejection unless such 
imperfections render the panel unfit for use. 


6.2 Dimensions 


The overall dimensions of the sandwich panels, when 
measured shall conform to as given in Table 1 subject 
to tolerances mentioned in Table 2. The minimum 
indentation depth shall be 10 mm for jointing system 
as shown in Fig. 4. 


6.2.1 Tolerance on Shape 


6.2.1.1 Tolerance on straightness of edge 


The tolerance on the straightness of the edge shall be 
3 mm per metre when measured in accordance with the 
method as specified in 6.2.1.1.1. 


6.2.1.1.1 The straightness of the edges and ends of 
lightweight concrete sandwich panel shall be verified 
against a straight edge not less than the full length of 
the lightweight concrete sandwich panel. If the edge 
on the end of lightweight concrete sandwich panel is 
convex, it shall be held against the straight edge in 
such a way as to give approximately equal gap at each 
end. The largest gap between the straight edge and the 
edge shall be measured to the nearest millimetre and 
recorded. 


6.2.1.2 Tolerance on squareness of edge 


The tolerance on squareness of the edge shall be 
4 mm per metre when measured in accordance with the 
method as specified in 6.2.1.2.1. 


FACING 
SHEET 


FIG. 4 TYPICAL DETAIL OF JOINTING SYSTEM IN SANDWICH PANEL 


6.2.1.2.1 The squareness of lightweight concrete 
sandwich panel shall be checked with a 
600 mm x 600 mm square, by applying one arm of 
the square to the sandwich panel and measuring to 
the nearest millimetre the gap between the other arm 
of the square. 


6.3 Density 

The density of sandwich panel when tested as per 
Annex B shall be between 500 kg/m? and 1 000 kg/m’. 
6.4 Bending Strength 


The bending strength of sandwich panel shall be 
determined by either of the two method given in 6.4.1 
and 6.4.2. 


6.4.1 Three Point Loading 


When tested in accordance with the method given 
in Annex C, the minimum bending strength of the 
sandwich panels shall be as specified in Table 3.

6.6 Optional Tests 


Following optional tests may be carried out as per the 
mutual agreement between the manufacturer and the 
purchaser based on the requirement of application of 
the sandwich panels. 


6.6.1 Axial Compression Load 


The minimum value of the axial compression load shall 
be 100 kN/m for 50 mm thickness and 125 kN/m for 
75 mm and 100 mm thick sandwich panel, when tested 
according to Annex F. 


6.6.2 Tensile Strength 


The minimum tensile strength perpendicular to 
surface shall be 0.25 N/mm? for 50 mm thickness and 
0.20 N/mm? for 75 mm and 100 mm thick sandwich 
panel, when tested according to IS 2380 (Part 5). 


6.6.3 Screw Withdrawal Strength 


The minimum screw withdrawal strength of sandwich 
panel shall be 0.3 kN, when tested according to IS 2380 
(Part 14). 


6.6.4 Sound Transmission 


The minimum sound transmission shall be 32 dB for 
50 mm thickness and 36 dB for 75 mm and 100 mm 
thick sandwich panel, when tested according to IS 9901 
(Part 3). 


6.6.5 Thermal Conductivity 


The maximum value of the thermal conductivity shall 
be 0.35 W/m-K for 50 mm thickness and 0.30 W/m-K 
for 75 and 100 mm thick sandwich panel when tested 
according to IS 3346. 


6.6.6 Fire Rating 


The minimum fire resistance rating shall be 60 min for 
50 mm thick; 120 min for 75 mm and 100 mm thick 
sandwich panel, when tested according to IS/ISO 834 
(Part 8). 


IS 17908 : 2023 


7 SAMPLING 


7.1 Lot 


In any consignment, all the sandwich panel of same 
construction having the same size and thickness, 
manufactured under similar condition in one day shall 
be grouped together to constitute a lot. 


The sandwich panels shall be selected from a lot at 
random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, 
the procedure given in IS 4905 shall be followed. The 
number of sandwich panel to be selected from the lot 
depends upon the lot size and shall be in accordance 
with Table 6. 


Table 6 Sampling of Sandwich Panels 
(Clauses 7.1, 8.1 and 8.2)

8 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


8.1 Sandwich panel selected in accordance with col 2 
and col 3 of Table 6 shall be inspected for visual 
defects, shape and dimension. A sandwich panel which 
is found to be not conforming to any one and more 
the requirements inspected for shall be considered 
defective. Maximum number of defectives permitted 
shall be as given in col 4 of Table 6. 


8.2 The lot which has been found as conforming to 
the 8.1 shall then be tested for bending strength, 
density and impact test. For this purpose, the number of 
sandwich panel to be selected shall be in accordance 
with col 2 and col 5 of Table 6. The lot shall be 
considered as conforming to these requirements if no 
defective is found. 


8.3 The lot shall be considered as conforming to the 
requirements of the specification if 8.1 and 8.2 are 
satisfied. 


8.4 Optional Requirements 


Acceptance criteria for optional requirements shall 
be as per mutual agreement by the purchaser and 
manufacturer. 


9 MANUFACTURER'S CERTIFICATE 


The manufacturer shall satisfy himselfthat the sandwich 
panels conform to the requirements of this standard and 
if requested shall supply a test certificate to this effect 
to the purchaser or his representative. 


10 MARKING 
Each sandwich panel shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; 

b) Size (L x W x T) of the sandwich panel; and 

c) Batch number and date of manufacture. 


11 BIS CERTIFICATION MARKING 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) 
may be marked with the Standard Mark.

ANNEX B 
(Clause 6.3) 
METHOD FOR THE DETERMINATION OF DENSITY 


B-1 PROCEDURE 


B-1.1 Three full size sandwich panels are taken. 
The dimensions of each panel shall be measured in 
millimetres. The panels shall then be weighed in 
kilograms (to the nearest 10 g) and the density of each 
panel sample is calculated. 


Density Mass of the pane! sample, а ЕС 
Volume of specimen, in m 


B-1.2 The average density of sandwich panel is the 
average of the densities of three panels. 


ANNEX C 
(Clause 6.4.1) 
METHOD OF TEST FOR THREE POINT LOAD BENDING STRENGTH 


C-1 BENDING STRENGTH 


C-1.1 Shapes and Dimensions of Test Pieces 


The test specimens shall be one specimen of 600 mm 
(L) х 100 mm (W) per panel. Sample shall be cut 
parallel to length and at least 200 mm away from edges. 


C-1.2 Apparatus 
The apparatus shall include the following items: 


a) Bending test machine (see Fig. 5) with an 
arrangement of a constant rate of deflection when 
applying the load and with an accuracy of + 1 96 
of the indicated value and comprising of the 
following: 


1) Two parallel supports, one rigid and one 
self-aligning, the distance between the 
supports shall be 500 mm. The upper faces of 
the supports shall be rounded and shall have a 
radius r between 3 mm and 25 mm. 


2) A loading bar identical to the two supports 
shall be situated above the specimen so that 
it is parallel to the supports and at an equal 
distance from each support. 


b 


wm 


A dial gauge reading to at least 0.1 mm with flat 
parallel metal jaws between 10 mm and 15 mm 
in diameter. 


C-1.3 Procedure 
Conditioning for equilibrium strength: 


Place the test specimens in controlled atmosphere 
of temperature of 27 + 2°C and relative humidity of 
50 + 10 percent for 24 + 2 h in such a manner that all 
faces are adequately ventilated. 


Place the test piece on the supports and load the test 
piece along its centre line by means of the loading bar. 
Load the specimen at 50 mm/min of deflection till the 
fracture occurs. 


Measure the thickness at two points. 


C-1.4 Expression and Interpretation of Results 


The bending strength, in N/mm’, is given by the 
formula 


Three point load bending strength = x 
e 


where 
P — the breaking load, in N; 
a — the distance between axes of supports, in mm; 
b — the width of the test piece, in mm; and 
e — the average thickness of the test piece, in mm. 
Distance between axis of supports, a — 500 mm. 


Assess the results against the requirement given in this 
standard.

r=3 mm to 25 mm

ANNEX E 
(Clause 6.5) 
IMPACT TESTS ON SANDWICH PANELS 


E-1 DETERMINATION OF SURFACE 
DAMAGE AND PERFORATION BY SMALL 
HARD BODY IMPACT 


E-1.1 Principle 


The test is to determine the resistance of the sandwich 
panel to damage from impact by small, hard objects. An 
impactor weighing 3 kg, with its head being a 50 mm 
diameter steel sphere, is swung to impact approximately 
perpendicularly to the face of the panel. The nature and 
extent of any damage to the panel is recorded. 


E-1.2 Specimen 


One sandwich panel shall be taken each for surface 
damage and perforation test. 


E-1.3 Apparatus 
The apparatus shall comprise the following: 


a) Impactor, having a head comprising a 50 mm 
diameter steel sphere mounted on a shaft not 
exceeding 20 mm diameter, weighed to bring the 
total mass of the impactor to 3 kg. The head shall 
be mounted as a pendulum 600 mm + | mm long, 
as shown in Fig. 7, from a bearing allowing it to 
swing freely in a vertical plane. 


Perpendicular to the plane of the specimen, but 
prevented from sideways movement, the arm of 
the pendulum shall be in the form of a metal rod 
or tube of approximate mass 1.3 kg/m length. 
The centre line of the pendulum arm shall meet 
the shaft of the impactor head 125 mm from the 
centre of the 50 mm sphere. At least 80 mm of 
the shaft of the impactor head, between the sphere 
and the attachment for the pendulum arm, shall be 
unobstructed to facilitate penetration. 


b 


wm 


Support frame for impactor, to allow impactor 
pendulum to be positioned as required for test, to 
hold pivot of pendulum in position during impact, 
and incorporating release mechanism to control 
pendulum’s angle of swing (see Fig. 7). 


С 


ме 


Measuring instrument, to measure the depth of 
indentation to the nearest 0.1 mm. 

NOTE — A convenient instrument for this purpose is a dial 
gauge mounted in the middle of a reference bar with a flattened 
knife edge at one end and a single rounded point contact at the 
other, forming a 100 mm bridge. 


E-1.4 Procedure 


Install the sandwich panel vertically with all edge fixed. 
Set up the test apparatus at the impact position, such 


11 


that when at rest the impactor just touches the face of 
the specimen as shown in (see Fig. 7). 


The impact position should be the center of sample. 
Raise the impactor to the angle of swing required for 
the impact energy being tested as shown in Table 8 and 
Table 9. 


Release the impactor once only and prevent it from 
bouncing.

E-1.5 Expression of Result 


No damage like indentation, delamination, fracture 
of surface, etc shall be found. There shall be no 
perforation. Measure the depth of indentation to the 
nearest 0.1 mm. 


E-2 DETERMINATION OF RESISTANCE TO 
DAMAGE BY LARGE SOFT BODY IMPACT 


E-2.1 Principle 


The test requires that the sandwich panel is subjected 
to impact from a soft body impactor in the form of 
a spheroconical bag capable of being swung at the 
specimen to determine the resistance to damage. The 
impact is applied by a bag, suspended from the test rig. 
The bag is positioned so that when at rest it just touches 
the face of the specimen at the point of intended impact. 


E-2.2 Specimen 


One sandwich panel shall be taken for damage test.

Fic. 7 APPARATUS FOR SMALL HARD Bopy IMPACT TEST 


E-2.3 Apparatus 
The apparatus shall be comprise the following: 


a) Spheroconical bag, having a mass of 50 + 0.5 kg 
made of eight sections sewn together. The bag 
when filled shall be in the form of a sphere of 
(400 + 1) mm diameter inscribed in a cone, the top 
of which is located at a distance of (400 + 1) mm 
from the centre of the sphere. The bottom of the 
bag is strengthened by a circular piece of leather 
of (120 + 1) mm diameter sewn into it. The top of 
the bag is slightly truncated in order to make an 
opening of (80 + 1) mm diameter. This opening 
is strengthened by a leather strip sewn onto the 
bag, to which are fixed four equidistant rings 
held together by a suspension ring. The bag is 
filled with hardened glass beads of (3 + 0.1) mm 
diameter (see Fig. 8). 


12 


b) Two pulleys and a suspension line, with means of 
attachment to the test rig. 


c) Winding and release mechanisms, for suspending 
the bag at the required drop height. 


d) Measuring instrument, capable of measuring, to 
an accuracy of 0.1 mm. 


E-2.4 Procedure 


Install the sandwich panel vertically with all edge fixed. 
The impact position should be the center of specimen. 


The level of impact energy shall be as given in 
Table 10. The line needs to be long enough to ensure 
that its angle to the plane of the specimen does not 
exceed 65°. Release the line allowing the bag to impact 
the specimen. Restrain the bag to prevent rebounding. 
Allow the specimen to stabilize for 5 min. Examine and 
record any damage to the specimen.

ANNEX F 
(Clause 6.6.1) 
METHOD FOR THE DETERMINATION OF AXIAL COMPRESSION LOAD TEST 


F-1 TEST SPECIMEN 


Three full size sandwich panels shall be taken and 
specimens of length 1 500 mm and width 300 mm shall 
be cut from each panel. 


F-2 APPARATUS 
The apparatus shall include an: 


a) Axial compression load test machine with an 
arrangement of a constant rate of loading with an 
accuracy of + | % of the indicated value. 


F-3 PROCEDURE 


Placed sample on axial compression machine as shown 
in Fig.10. Apply the load gradually till the panel breaks. 


F-4 Calculate axial strength as follows: 


Axial strength (kN / m) = a 
1000xW 
where 
ABL = Axial breaking load, in kg; and 
W = Width of specimen, in metre, m. 


F-5 EXPRESSION OF RESULT 


Report the test results as the average of three specimens 
in the following format: 


SI No. Size of Panel Axial Breaking Calculated Axial Remarks 
(Length x Width x Thickness) Load Strength Per meter 
mm kg kN/mm

IS 17908 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 53 (14917).
